arguments: Hash update forwards unvalidated caller buffer to an existing secure operation
message.text: Hash update forwards unvalidated caller buffer to an existing secure operation

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: the reported unvalidated caller buffer path is contradicted by dispatcher initialization that maps or copies nonzero client input before the hash interface receives it. Evidence: in MM-IOVEC builds nonzero in_vec entries are set from psa_map_invec and zero-length entries get NULL at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:70-76, while non-MM builds allocate scratch and read input into it before assigning in_vec[i].base at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:166-178; tfm_crypto_call_srv performs this initialization before dispatch at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:291-299, and the hash update then forwards that prepared in_vec[1] at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:196-199. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Validate in_vec[1].base before using it: allow NULL only when input_length is zero, otherwise return PSA_ERROR_PROGRAMMER_ERROR. If an invalid update should terminate the operation under the service contract, explicitly abort/release the operation; otherwise document that the handle remains valid after parameter errors.
properties.reasoning: For multipart hash update, the secure operation state is looked up before the input buffer is validated, and then the caller-controlled base and length are passed directly to psa_hash_update. If input_length is nonzero and in_vec[1].base is NULL or not a valid mapped client buffer, the secure service may fault or the lower layer may read unintended memory. This is particularly relevant because a malformed update can target an already allocated operation and may leave state lifetime/cleanup to the caller after an error.
